units.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a Python library for creating, reading, converting, and saving 3D scenes using formats such as .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, .3mf, and .fbx. It enables developers to build 3D content programmatically by instantiating primitives like Box, Sphere, and Cylinder, constructing custom meshes with Mesh, and assigning materials such as LambertMaterial or PbrMaterial. Users can manage scene structure through nodes, transforms, and animation clips, and export scenes to disk or in-memory streams. The library runs on Python 3.7 through 3.12, requires no external dependencies, and is distributed under the MIT license.
Load scenes from .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, and .3mf files using Scene.open() which auto-detects the format from the file extension or an explicit FileFormat instance.
Export scenes to .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, and .3mf formats using Scene.save() with format-specific save options provided by FileFormat.get_format_by_extension().create_save_options().

Construct meshes by adding control points and polygons via Mesh.control_points.add() and Mesh.create_polygon(), or convert parameterized primitives like Box and Sphere to editable meshes using their to_mesh() method.
Assign LambertMaterial or PbrMaterial to nodes by setting diffuse_color, ambient_color, emissive_color, albedo, metallic_factor, and roughness_factor properties directly on the material instance.
Traverse and manipulate scene graphs using Node.create_child_node() to build hierarchies, where each node holds an independent Transform for translation, rotation, and scaling operations.
Build keyframe animation using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence to define time-based transformations and properties for animated scenes.
Open an existing 3D file and inspect its geometry by reading the scene and traversing its nodes.
Build a 3D scene from scratch by creating primitives, assigning materials, and saving the result to a supported format.
Create scenes from scratch, assign materials, and export to glTF, STL, and 3MF formats using Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
Export a scene with a PBR material to text-based glTF and inspect the material JSON.
Export a triangle mesh to text-based STL using an in-memory stream.
Convert a Box primitive to a mesh and count its control points.
Build a cube mesh and export it to 3MF without compression.

The aspose-3d-foss package provides 3D scene manipulation through the aspose.threed.Scene class, which serves as the primary entry point for loading, saving, and inspecting 3D content, and aspose.threed.FileFormat, which enumerates supported import and export formats. The Scene class organizes content in a hierarchy of Node objects, each with a Transform, optional Mesh entities, and Material assignments.

The aspose.threed.Scene class provides Scene.open() and Scene.save() methods to load and write 3D scenes, and exposes Scene.root_node, Scene.animation_clips, Scene.library, and Scene.sub_scenes to inspect and modify the scene graph.

The aspose.threed.Node class represents an element in the scene hierarchy, exposing Node.transform for position and orientation, Node.child_nodes for the tree structure, and Node.entities to hold Mesh or other Entity instances.
The aspose.threed.Mesh class stores geometry via control_points and polygons, and can be constructed from Primitive shapes or converted from an Entity using the to_mesh method.

The aspose.threed.shading.LambertMaterial class defines a simple shading model with diffuse_color, while aspose.threed.shading.PbrMaterial extends this with metallic_factor and roughness_factor for physically based rendering.
The aspose.threed.AnimationClip class holds animation data through AnimationNode and KeyframeSequence entries, and Scene.animation_clips exposes the collection of clips attached to a scene.
The A3DObject class represents a base object in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python that supports named properties and can be queried for its properties.
The AnimationChannel class represents a single animated property channel that holds keyframe sequences and default values for interpolation.
The AnimationClip class represents a container for animation data that defines a time range and contains animation nodes.
The AnimationNode class represents a node in an animation hierarchy that binds animation channels to scene nodes and supports sub-animations.
The AssetInfo class holds metadata about a 3D asset such as author, creation time, coordinate system, and unit scale factor.
The BindPoint class represents a binding point that associates a scene node with animation channels for skeletal animation.
The BonePose class represents the pose of a bone in local or world space using a transformation matrix.
The Box class represents a box primitive with configurable length, height, and segment counts.
The Camera class represents a camera entity that defines a view frustum for rendering.
The Circle class represents a circular primitive defined by its radius and segment count.
The Curve class represents a parametric curve entity in three-dimensional space.
The CustomObject class represents a user-defined object that extends the A3DObject base class.
The Cylinder class represents a cylindrical primitive with configurable radius, height, and segment counts.
The Dish class represents a dish-shaped primitive defined by its radii and segment counts.
The Ellipse class represents an elliptical primitive defined by its radii and segment count.
The Entity class represents a renderable or transformable object in a scene that can be assigned to a node.
The Extrapolation class defines how animation values are computed outside the defined keyframe range.
The ExtrapolationType class defines the enumeration of supported extrapolation modes for animation.
The FileFormat class provides methods to identify and work with supported 3D file formats by extension.
The Frustum class represents a viewing frustum primitive used for camera projection definitions.
The Geometry class represents a geometric entity that can be used to define shapes and meshes.
The GlobalTransform class represents a global transformation matrix applied to a scene object.
The INamedObject class defines an interface for objects that can be assigned a name.
The ImageRenderOptions class holds settings for rendering a scene to an image format.
The Interpolation class defines the enumeration of supported interpolation methods for animation keyframes.
The KeyFrame class represents a single keyframe with a time value and associated data.
The KeyframeSequence class represents a sequence of keyframes used for animating a property.
The Light class represents a light entity that inherits from Camera and defines illumination properties.
The LinearExtrusion class represents a 3D shape created by extruding a 2D profile along a straight path.
The Mesh class represents a polygonal mesh geometry composed of vertices and polygons.
The Node class represents a transformable object in the scene hierarchy that can hold an entity.
The Plane class represents a planar primitive defined by its size and segment counts.
The PolygonBuilder class provides utilities for constructing polygonal meshes from geometric primitives.
The Pose class represents a snapshot of transformation data for a set of nodes in a scene.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python version 26.1.0 supports reading and writing OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA 3D formats, and provides core scene graph inspection and manipulation capabilities through the Scene, Node, and Entity APIs.

No file format registers an importer or exporter for PDF, PLY, RVM, U3D, JT, AMF, HTML5, A3DW, USD, or Draco in this build — PdfSaveOptions, PlyLoadOptions, DracoSaveOptions, and similar option classes exist as public types, but Scene.open() and Scene.save() cannot detect or dispatch any of these extensions, and raise a RuntimeError if you try.

FBX support is experimental: FbxImporter has a real, working ASCII/binary tokenizer and parser, but no bundled test opens a real .fbx fixture through it, and FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() both raise NotImplementedError outright, so FBX is import-only at best.
COLLADA import works, but COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() because IOService's exporter lookup fails before it ever reaches ColladaExporter.

Always import a format's load/save options class from its own format submodule, never from the shared top-level aspose.threed.formats package — for OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA specifically, the top-level package name resolves to a broken duplicate with no working base class, which format detection silently rejects.

Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module (Renderer, RenderFactory, Viewport, and related classes) raise NotImplementedError, and Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction, so an image-backed texture cannot be created.

Watermark.encode_watermark() and decode_watermark() and every TransformBuilder method raise NotImplementedError, Mesh.do_boolean(), union(), difference(), and intersect() raise NotImplementedError, NurbsCurve.evaluate() and NurbsSurface.to_mesh() raise NotImplementedError, PointCloud.from_geometry() and from_geometry_with_density() raise NotImplementedError, and AxisSystem raises NotImplementedError on every method, including construction.
Install the package in editable mode and run the test suite using the repository's own assets.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python provides open-source 3D processing capabilities, while Aspose.3D commercial edition adds advanced features such as support for more file formats, enhanced performance, and commercial licensing.
